what: how bench/results/smoke-1.20.2/checks.json was produced, so a reader can tell what it measures and what it does not
upstream: oscardvs/zoteus at c386e835a2ef90b539b611168130c8540cd55fe5 (v1.20.2 tag), checked out by `make upstream-checkout` into fork/, built with `npm ci && npm run build` on 2026-09-17
host: the author's Linux workstation; no desktop Zotero was running, so the library transport was forced to the Zotero Web API (`ZOTEUS_LOCAL=off`, a read-only API key for user 95318 from the operator's key store); the on-device embedder ran from a standalone transformers.js install passed as `--transformers-path`
index_under_test: a 40-item, metadata-only build made by this run against the real library (`zotero_index action:"build" limit:40 own_words:false fulltext:false`, 40 passages, 40 vectors, `local:Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`), because no schema-1 index carrying vectors survives on this host and a 984 MB vector-less schema-1 index would have hit the v1.20.2 semantic refusal on `hasVectors` rather than the ladder
restamp: for R23-previous-schema-migrates-in-place the copy handed to `--index` had its `meta.schemaVersion` set from 2 to 1 by hand; the ladder's one rung (2, rebuild passages_fts under the diacritic-preserving tokenizer, re-embed nothing) was therefore walked on a file of this build's own shape, not on a v1.12-era artifact. What the check reads back — the stamp before and after, row and vector counts, the served counts, the notice text, the probe query's hits — all came off the run
not_measured: R10-local-embedder's `cloud: true` is the library transport the host forced, not the embedder: `whoami.embeddings.effective` and `status.embedder` both read `local`. Nothing here speaks for the desktop local-API path, the full-text pass, own words, or the keyed attachment map (#78), none of which this run exercised
acceptance: bench/results/smoke-1.20.2/acceptance-zoteus.json, if present beside this file, is the acceptance layer's own artifact for the same build under the account posture; its declaration block records its inputs
